mapping_path <- "../../../Input/Harmonized_Datasets/Targeted_Analyte_Category_Mapping.csv"
targeted_mapping <- read_targeted_analyte_mapping(mapping_path)

plot_categories <- c(
  "TraceElements", "Phenols", "Phthalates", "PAH", "PCB", "Parabens",
  "Smoking", "Pesticides", "VOCs", "FlameRetardants", "PFAS"
)

targeted_category_lookup <- targeted_mapping %>%
  dplyr::filter(Category %in% plot_categories) %>%
  dplyr::select(Code, Category) %>%
  dplyr::distinct()

theme_codes <- targeted_theme_codes(targeted_mapping)
get_theme <- function(category_name) {
  if (category_name %in% names(theme_codes)) unique(theme_codes[[category_name]]) else character()
}

Trace_Elements_Theme <- get_theme("TraceElements")
Phenols_Theme <- get_theme("Phenols")
PAH_Theme <- get_theme("PAH")
Phthalates_Theme <- get_theme("Phthalates")
Parabens_Theme <- get_theme("Parabens")
Smoking_Theme <- get_theme("Smoking")
Inflam_Theme <- get_theme("Inflammation")
Pesticide_Theme <- get_theme("Pesticides")
VOC_Theme <- get_theme("VOCs")
OXID_Theme <- get_theme("OxidativeStress")
PFAS_Theme <- get_theme("PFAS")
Flame_Retardant_Theme <- get_theme("FlameRetardants")
PCB_Theme <- get_theme("PCB")
Other_Theme <- character()

add_plot_category <- function(data, code_col = "Outcome") {
  dplyr::left_join(data, targeted_category_lookup, by = stats::setNames("Code", code_col))
}

Results Parse Function
-----
```{r}
Parse_Results <- function(Results_List = Child_SDOH_Metab_Quantile_Results_SexByStudy,Cohort_Meta = Cohort_Meta){
  
  
  if(Cohort_Meta == T){
    
    All_Res <- list()
  
  for(i in seq_along(Results_List)){
    
    curr_study <- Results_List[[i]]
    
             #print(i)
      
         curr_results <- try(curr_study[[1]][["Regression_Results"]] %>% 
             dplyr::filter(Variable != "(Intercept)") %>% 
             mutate(
            Study = names(Results_List[i])) )

         if(is.character(curr_results)){
           next
         }
         
         All_Res[[i]] <- curr_results
        
  }
  Final_Res <- bind_rows(All_Res)
    
  }else{
  
  
  All_Res <- list()
  
  for(i in seq_along(Results_List)){
    
    curr_study <- Results_List[[i]]
    
    curr_study_all_res <- list() 
             #print(i)

    for(j in seq_along(curr_study)){
      
         curr_results <- try(curr_study[[j]][[1]][["Regression_Results"]] %>% 
             dplyr::filter(Variable != "(Intercept)") %>% 
             mutate(
            Study = names(Results_List[i])) )

         if(is.character(curr_results)){
           next
         }
         
         curr_study_all_res[[j]] <- curr_results
        
      }
      
      curr_study_all_res <-  curr_study_all_res[lengths(curr_study_all_res) != 0]

    Results <- bind_rows(curr_study_all_res)
    
      All_Res[[i]] <- Results

  }
  Final_Res <- bind_rows(All_Res)
  }
# FDR SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 2.8).
# p.adjust() used to run INSIDE the loop above, correcting across the handful of
# coefficients in a single model rather than across the whole scan. It now runs
# once, on the bound results, via apply_scan_fdr() in harmonization_helpers.R.
# That helper also asserts the p-values are not all NA, which is what happens
# when the upstream fit was run with summary_R < 25 (see audit section 1.5).
  return(apply_scan_fdr(Final_Res, what = "Location_Compare / Final_Res"))
}
```


Process Results
----------

```{r}
Process_Quant_Results <- function(Mat_Quant_Results) {
  All_Outcome_Results_Mat <- list()
  
  for (i in seq_along(Mat_Quant_Results)) {
    Curr_Reg_Results <- Mat_Quant_Results[[i]]
    
    if (!is.list(Curr_Reg_Results) || length(Curr_Reg_Results) == 0) {
      next
    }
    
    Curr_Reg_Results <- Curr_Reg_Results[
      vapply(Curr_Reg_Results, function(x) is.list(x) && length(x) > 0, logical(1))
    ]
    
    All_Reg_Results <- list()
    for (j in seq_along(Curr_Reg_Results)) {
      Res <- Curr_Reg_Results[[j]][["Regression_Results"]]
      
      if (is.null(Res) || !is.data.frame(Res)) {
        next
      }
      
      All_Reg_Results[[j]] <- Res
    }
    
    if (length(All_Reg_Results) == 0) {
      next
    }
    
    All_Reg_Results <- bind_rows(All_Reg_Results) %>%
      filter(!str_detect(Variable, "(Intercept)"))
    
    All_Outcome_Results_Mat[[i]] <- All_Reg_Results
    names(All_Outcome_Results_Mat)[i] <- unique(All_Reg_Results$Outcome)
  }
  
  All_Outcome_Results_Mat_Df <- bind_rows(All_Outcome_Results_Mat)
# FDR SCOPE (fixed 2026-08-11, CODE_AUDIT_2026-08-11.md section 2.8).
# p.adjust() used to run INSIDE the loop above, correcting across the handful of
# coefficients in a single model rather than across the whole scan. It now runs
# once, on the bound results, via apply_scan_fdr() in harmonization_helpers.R.
# That helper also asserts the p-values are not all NA, which is what happens
# when the upstream fit was run with summary_R < 25 (see audit section 1.5).
  return(apply_scan_fdr(All_Outcome_Results_Mat_Df, what = "Location_Compare / All_Outcome_Results_Mat_Df"))
}

```

R2 Bar Plots
-----



```{r}

# --- pick a nested model sequence (order matters) ---
# MODEL USED BY THIS PANEL (changed 2026-08-11).
#
# Was c("Study", "Center", "Year", "Location_Region") -- a nested decomposition
# that built the bar as cumulative increments across four covariate sets, and
# notably did NOT include the Location model at all, despite the panel being
# titled "Distributional Contribution of Location" in All_Patchplots.Rmd.
#
# The manuscript uses Exposure ~ Location, so the panel now reads that model.
# With a single entry the decomposition below degenerates gracefully: contrib =
# mean_R2 - lag(default 0) = mean_R2, so each category gets one bar equal to its
# mean pseudo-R2 for Location, and `component` reads "Baseline: Location".
#
# Restore the old vector to get the nested-decomposition version back.
study_focus_seq <- c("Location")
available_model_seq <- All_R2_Data %>%
  dplyr::filter(Model_Type %in% study_focus_seq) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(Model_Type) %>%
  dplyr::pull(Model_Type)

model_seq <- study_focus_seq[study_focus_seq %in% available_model_seq]

df_f <- All_R2_Data %>% 
  filter(Model_Type %in% model_seq) %>% 
  group_by( Category,Model_Type) %>% 
  #dplyr::filter(Study == "CCREOH") %>% 
  summarise(mean_R2 = mean(plot_R2, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%  
  arrange(Category, match(Model_Type, model_seq)) %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  mutate(
    # Force baseline to 0 and ensure monotonic increase
    #mean_R2 = cummax(mean_R2),  
    total_R2 = max(mean_R2, na.rm = TRUE),
    contrib = pmax(mean_R2 - lag(mean_R2, default = 0), 0),
    component = if_else(row_number() == 1,
                        paste0("Baseline: ", Model_Type),
                        paste0("+ ", Model_Type))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() 



mypal <- paletteer_d("ggsci::springfield_simpsons")

```

exposome_palette <- c(
  "FlameRetardants" = "#FED439FF",  # yellow
  "PAH"             = "#709AE1FF",  # blue
  "Parabens"        = "#8A9197FF",  # gray
  "PCBs"            = "#D2AF81FF",  # tan
  "Pesticide"       = "#FD7446FF",  # orange
  "PFAS"            = "#D5E4A2FF",  # light green
  "Phenols"         = "#197EC0FF",  # deep blue
  "Phthalates"      = "#F05C3BFF",  # red-orange
  "Smoking"         = "#46732EFF",  # dark green
  "TraceElements"  = "#71D0F5FF",  # light blue
  "VOC"             = "#370335FF"   # dark purple
)


pool_colors <- paletteer_d("ggsci::springfield_simpsons")

pool <-paletteer_d("ggsci::springfield_simpsons")

# The 7 levels you want to color
comp_levels <- c("Study","Location","Year","Center",
               "Location_Region","Location_Center","Location_Year")

comp_levels <- model_seq

# Name the first 7 colors by your levels
mypal <- setNames(pool[seq_along(comp_levels)], comp_levels)


comp_levels <- names(mypal)
df_plot <- df_f%>%
  mutate(
    Category  = fct_reorder(Category, total_R2),
    component = factor(Model_Type, levels = comp_levels)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Category) %>%
  arrange(Category, component, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  # compute stack geometry
  mutate(
    xmin = cumsum(lag(contrib, default = 0)),
    xmax = xmin + contrib,
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    frac = contrib / sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # flag largest slice (break ties deterministically by first factor level)
  mutate(is_max = contrib == max(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(mypal))) %>%
  # BASELINE ROW OF THE STACK (generalised 2026-08-11). This was a hardcoded
  # dplyr::filter(Model_Type == "Study"), which selected the first entry of the
  # old study_focus_seq. With the sequence set to c("Location") it matched
  # nothing and the panel rendered completely empty -- a silent blank figure,
  # not an error. Keyed to the sequence itself so the two cannot diverge again.
  dplyr::filter(Model_Type == model_seq[1])



totals <- df_plot %>%
  group_by(Category) %>%
  summarise(total = sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")


# 2) Beautiful stacked horizontal bars + total marker
r2_barplot <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = total_R2, y = Category, fill = Category)) +
  geom_bar(stat="identity", width=0.5) +

  # Add label only to largest bar in each Category
  # geom_text(

  #   inherit.aes = FALSE

  scale_fill_manual(values = exposome_palette, drop = FALSE) +

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}   # interactive View() only; cannot run under render()
df_f%>%
  mutate(
    Category  = fct_reorder(Category, total_R2),
    component = factor(Model_Type, levels = comp_levels)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Category) %>%
  arrange(Category, component, .by_group = TRUE) %>%
  # compute stack geometry
  mutate(
    xmin = cumsum(lag(contrib, default = 0)),
    xmax = xmin + contrib,
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    frac = contrib / sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # flag largest slice (break ties deterministically by first factor level)
  mutate(is_max = contrib == max(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(component = factor(component, levels = names(mypal))) %>% 
  dplyr::filter(Model_Type == "Study") %>% 
  View
```

```{r, eval=FALSE, purl=FALSE}   # interactive View() only; cannot run under render()
df_f %>% 
  mutate(
    xmin = cumsum(lag(contrib, default = 0)),
    xmax = xmin + contrib,
    xmid = (xmin + xmax) / 2,
    frac = contrib / sum(contrib, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Category,All_Vars) %>% 
  summarise(mean_totalr2 = mean(mean_R2),
            mean_contrib = mean(contrib),
            mean_frac = mean(frac)) %>% 
  View
```
